GET-QUARTERLY-CLEANUP-REVIEW.ps1.name: Review Account Cleanup
details: A review list, not approval to delete accounts or remove access.
Missing checks remain unresolved.
GET-QUARTERLY-CLEANUP-REVIEW.ps1.objective: Review accounts, mailbox access, and licenses for cleanup.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph and Exchange Online PowerShell with authorized tenant access.

GET-STALE-SIGNIN-REVIEW.ps1.name: Review Stale Sign-ins
details: Uses recorded Entra activity, not proof that an account is unused.
Missing sign-in history stays unknown.
GET-STALE-SIGNIN-REVIEW.ps1.objective: Find enabled accounts with old or unavailable Entra sign-in activity.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

INVOKE-DISABLE-ACCOUNTS.ps1.name: Disable User Accounts
details: Synced accounts are disabled in AD; cloud accounts in Entra.
Review the targets before confirming.
INVOKE-DISABLE-ACCOUNTS.ps1.objective: Disable selected user accounts in AD or Entra after approval.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

INVOKE-DELETE-ACCOUNTS.ps1.name: Delete User Accounts
details: Review dependencies and retention before deleting an account.
Deletion requires explicit confirmation.
INVOKE-DELETE-ACCOUNTS.ps1.objective: Delete approved user accounts from their authoritative directory.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

INVOKE-ASSIGN-LICENSES.ps1.name: Assign User Licenses
details: Choose a license and review the affected users before confirming.
Review failed assignments separately.
INVOKE-ASSIGN-LICENSES.ps1.objective: Assign a selected Microsoft 365 license to approved users.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

INVOKE-REMOVE-LICENSES.ps1.name: Remove User Licenses
details: License removal can affect services and retained data.
Review the selected licenses and users before confirming.
INVOKE-REMOVE-LICENSES.ps1.objective: Remove selected Microsoft 365 licenses from approved users.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

RESOLVE-NAMES-TO-UPNS.ps1.name: Find User UPNs
details: Review ambiguous or missing matches before using the list in another tool.
RESOLVE-NAMES-TO-UPNS.ps1.objective: Find user sign-in names from names, email addresses, or a list.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-ACCOUNT-STATUS.ps1.name: Get User Account Status
details: Missing sign-in history does not mean an account is inactive.
GET-ACCOUNT-STATUS.ps1.objective: Show whether selected accounts are enabled and when they last signed in.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-DISTRIBUTION-GROUP-MEMBERS.ps1.name: Get Distribution Group Members
details: For distribution groups in Exchange Online.
Nested groups are not a complete access review.
GET-DISTRIBUTION-GROUP-MEMBERS.ps1.objective: List direct members of selected Exchange distribution groups.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-GROUP-MEMBERS.ps1.name: Get Group Members
details: Checks the group in Exchange, Entra or AD.
Shows direct members, not a complete access review.
GET-GROUP-MEMBERS.ps1.objective: List direct members of selected groups.
preparation: Requires Exchange Online PowerShell; Entra or AD results also need access to that directory.

GET-USER-GROUPS.ps1.name: Get User Groups
details: Lists direct groups, not every source of access.
AD and Entra results are separate; failed coverage stays unresolved.
GET-USER-GROUPS.ps1.objective: List the selected users' direct groups in AD and Entra.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.
For AD results, use a domain-connected Windows computer with the AD tools installed.

INVOKE-REMOVE-USER-GROUPS.ps1.name: Remove User Groups
details: Removes memberships, not the groups themselves.
Some managed or protected memberships must be handled separately.
INVOKE-REMOVE-USER-GROUPS.ps1.objective: Remove selected users from eligible AD and Entra groups.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

INVOKE-CREATE-DYNAMIC-LICENSE-GROUP.ps1.name: Create Dynamic License Group
INVOKE-CREATE-DYNAMIC-LICENSE-GROUP.ps1.input: Tenant and group settings + tenant ID
details: Creates membership based on assigned licenses; does not assign licenses to the group.
Review the membership rule before creating the group.
INVOKE-CREATE-DYNAMIC-LICENSE-GROUP.ps1.objective: Create a group that automatically includes users with assigned licenses.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-TENANT-GROUP-OWNERS.ps1.name: Get Group Owners
details: Missing owners and failed checks are different findings.
GET-TENANT-GROUP-OWNERS.ps1.objective: List group owners and identify groups without an assigned owner.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph and Exchange Online PowerShell with authorized tenant access.

GET-MAILBOX-PERMISSIONS.ps1.name: Get Mailbox Permissions
details: Reviews forwarding, delegates and inbox rules.
Investigate unexpected access before removing it.
GET-MAILBOX-PERMISSIONS.ps1.objective: Review forwarding, delegated access, and inbox rules for selected mailboxes.
preparation: Requires Exchange Online PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-MAILBOX-SECURITY-SNAPSHOT.ps1.name: Get Mailbox Security
details: Use for a focused review of one mailbox.
Unresolved checks are not evidence that the mailbox is clear.
GET-MAILBOX-SECURITY-SNAPSHOT.ps1.objective: Review one mailbox for unexpected access, forwarding, and suspicious rules.
preparation: Requires Exchange Online PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-MAILBOX-FORWARDING.ps1.name: Get Mailbox Forwarding
details: Unexpected forwarding needs investigation before changes.
GET-MAILBOX-FORWARDING.ps1.objective: Show where selected mailboxes forward incoming email.
preparation: Requires Exchange Online PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

INVOKE-LITIGATION-HOLD.ps1.name: Set Litigation Hold
details: Confirm the retention decision and required licensing first.
Applies an unlimited hold after review.
INVOKE-LITIGATION-HOLD.ps1.objective: Enable an unlimited litigation hold on approved mailboxes.
preparation: Requires Exchange Online PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

IR-INVOKE-EMAIL-RECOVERY.ps1.name: Incident Response: Restore Email
details: Moves messages between folders in a mailbox you can access.
Delivery-trace exports are not recovery sources. Review the source folder before confirming.
IR-INVOKE-EMAIL-RECOVERY.ps1.objective: Restore previously moved email to the selected mailbox.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.
You need access to the target mailbox and folders; an admin role alone is not enough.

ir-risk-assessment.ps1.name: BEC: Assess User Risk
ir-risk-assessment.ps1.input: User sign-in address and Microsoft 365 domain or tenant ID
details: Use the approved support computer and keep the workflow in one PowerShell window.
Review findings and unavailable checks before deciding on containment.
ir-risk-assessment.ps1.objective: Review one user's account and mailbox before choosing a response.
preparation: Use the approved Windows support computer with Microsoft.Graph.Authentication 2.x and ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.2+.

ir-contain-eradicate.ps1.name: BEC: Contain and Clean Up
ir-contain-eradicate.ps1.input: User sign-in address and Microsoft 365 domain or tenant ID
details: Use the same PowerShell window as assessment.
Maintain containment until cleanup and recovery are approved.
Temporary passwords can remain in terminal capture/transcripts. The operator confirms trusted MFA methods.
ir-contain-eradicate.ps1.objective: Contain and clean up one compromised account after approval.
preparation: Use the approved Windows support computer with Microsoft.Graph.Authentication 2.x and ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.2+.

IR-GET-DATA-EXFIL-ACTIVITY.ps1.name: Incident Response: Review File Activity
details: Activity can suggest exposure; it does not prove data theft.
Log availability limits the review.
IR-GET-DATA-EXFIL-ACTIVITY.ps1.objective: Review a user's file activity for possible data exposure.
preparation: Requires Exchange Online PowerShell and permission to read the requested records.

IR-GET-IP-TRACE.ps1.name: Incident Response: Trace IP Activity
details: An IP match needs context before attributing activity to a person.
IR-GET-IP-TRACE.ps1.objective: Find tenant audit activity associated with a selected IP address.
preparation: Requires Exchange Online PowerShell and permission to read the requested records.

IR-GET-TENANT-EMAIL-SEARCH.ps1.name: Incident Response: Trace Email Delivery
details: Searches delivery records, not message bodies or attachments.
Does not create a recovery folder or restore email.
IR-GET-TENANT-EMAIL-SEARCH.ps1.objective: Find email delivery records by sender, recipient, or IP address.
preparation: Requires Exchange Online PowerShell and permission to read the requested records.

IR-GET-THREAT-INTEL-ACTIVITY.ps1.name: Incident Response: Check IP Reputation
IR-GET-THREAT-INTEL-ACTIVITY.ps1.input: Public IP / TXT + provider API keys
details: Sends selected public IPs to VirusTotal or AbuseIPDB.
Reputation is context, not a verdict on compromise.
IR-GET-THREAT-INTEL-ACTIVITY.ps1.objective: Check selected public IP addresses against external reputation services.
preparation: Have an API key for each provider you enable.

IR-GET-TIMELINE-BUILDER.ps1.name: Incident Response: Build Incident Timeline
details: Combines supplied evidence; it does not collect missing events.
When event time is unavailable, labels the file’s modified time separately. Check time zones and gaps before drawing conclusions.
IR-GET-TIMELINE-BUILDER.ps1.objective: Combine supplied incident evidence into a timeline.

IR-GET-TOKEN-DECODE.ps1.name: Incident Response: Decode Token
details: Decodes locally without sending the token to a service.
A decoded token is not proof of authenticity or current access.
IR-GET-TOKEN-DECODE.ps1.objective: Read a token's contents locally without sending it online.

IR-GET-TOKEN-REPLAY-CHECK.ps1.name: Incident Response: Review Token Replay
details: Looks for indicators that need investigation, not a definitive compromise verdict.
Missing logs limit the result.
IR-GET-TOKEN-REPLAY-CHECK.ps1.objective: Review sign-ins for indicators of token replay or session theft.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-SHARED-MAILBOX-SIGNIN-AUDIT.ps1.name: Audit Shared Mailbox Sign-ins
details: Review unexpected direct sign-ins separately from delegated mailbox use.
GET-SHARED-MAILBOX-SIGNIN-AUDIT.ps1.objective: Find sign-in activity associated with shared mailboxes.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-APP-REGISTRATION-AUDIT.ps1.name: Audit App Registrations
details: Review unfamiliar apps and expiring credentials with their owners.
GET-APP-REGISTRATION-AUDIT.ps1.objective: Review registered apps, ownership, and credential expiry dates.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-CONDITIONAL-ACCESS-GAPS.ps1.name: Review Conditional Access
details: Use the tenant ID requested by the script, not just a domain name.
Findings identify review areas; they do not prove policy coverage.
GET-CONDITIONAL-ACCESS-GAPS.ps1.objective: Find Conditional Access settings and exclusions that need review.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-DEVICE-CODE-EXPOSURE.ps1.name: Review Device Code Exposure
details: Reviews policy exposure rather than proving an attack occurred.
GET-DEVICE-CODE-EXPOSURE.ps1.objective: Review policies for gaps in device-code sign-in protection.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-GUEST-APP-CONSENT-AUDIT.ps1.name: Audit Guest App Consent
details: Review permissions with an owner before removing consent.
GET-GUEST-APP-CONSENT-AUDIT.ps1.objective: Review guest users and their app permissions.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-MFA-SECURITY-AUDIT.ps1.name: Audit MFA Security
details: Review registration and policy findings together.
Missing evidence is not a clean MFA result.
GET-MFA-SECURITY-AUDIT.ps1.objective: Review MFA registration and the policies intended to protect sign-ins.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-SECURE-SCORE-SNAPSHOT.ps1.name: Get Secure Score
details: A score is a prioritization aid, not proof that the tenant is secure.
GET-SECURE-SCORE-SNAPSHOT.ps1.objective: Show the tenant's latest Microsoft Secure Score.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-SERVICE-PRINCIPAL-OWNERS.ps1.name: Get Enterprise App Owners
details: Ownerless apps need an accountable owner before changes.
GET-SERVICE-PRINCIPAL-OWNERS.ps1.objective: List enterprise app owners and identify apps without an owner.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-SIGNIN-ANOMALIES.ps1.name: Review Sign-in Anomalies
details: Review unusual activity in context before containment.
GET-SIGNIN-ANOMALIES.ps1.objective: Find unusual sign-in activity that needs investigation.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-TRANSPORT-RULES-AUDIT.ps1.name: Audit Mail Flow Rules
details: Review rule intent and business impact before making changes.
GET-TRANSPORT-RULES-AUDIT.ps1.objective: Review mail flow rules for settings that need attention.
preparation: Requires Exchange Online PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

JOIN-COMPUTER-TO-DOMAIN.ps1.name: Join Computer to Domain
details: Run as administrator; the computer must reach the domain.
Plan for restart and sign-in changes.
JOIN-COMPUTER-TO-DOMAIN.ps1.objective: Join the current computer to the selected AD domain.

DEPLOY-TCPIP-PRINTER.ps1.name: Install Network Printer
details: Have the printer address ready.
DEPLOY-TCPIP-PRINTER.ps1.objective: Install a network printer using its address and selected driver.
preparation: Have the approved printer driver installed and permission to add printers.

BACKUP-USER-PROFILE.ps1.name: Back Up User Profile
details: Check the destination and available space before starting.
Review skipped and failed copies before relying on the backup.
BACKUP-USER-PROFILE.ps1.objective: Copy selected user-profile folders to a backup location.

TEST-POWERSHELL-READINESS.ps1.name: Check M365 PowerShell Readiness
details: Reviews prerequisites without installing them.
TEST-POWERSHELL-READINESS.ps1.objective: Check this computer for Microsoft 365 PowerShell prerequisites.

GET-FOLDER-INVENTORY.ps1.name: Review Folder Contents
details: Shows files, signatures and available Git indicators in the chosen folder.
Does not compare content hashes to find duplicate files.
GET-FOLDER-INVENTORY.ps1.objective: Review a folder's files, script signatures, and Git status.

INSTALL-M365-MODULES.ps1.name: Install M365 Modules
details: Installs or updates modules for the current Windows user.
No tenant configuration is changed.
INSTALL-M365-MODULES.ps1.objective: Install or update the selected Microsoft 365 PowerShell modules.

TEST-SENSITIVE-DATA.ps1.name: Check Sensitive Data
details: Findings need review; a clean scan is not proof that all sensitive information is absent.
TEST-SENSITIVE-DATA.ps1.objective: Scan selected files for potentially sensitive information before sharing.

RESET-M365-SESSION.ps1.name: Reset M365 Session
details: Run in the session you want to disconnect.
Tenant configuration is not changed.
RESET-M365-SESSION.ps1.objective: Disconnect Microsoft 365 services in the current PowerShell window.

UPDATE-WINDOWS-APPS.ps1.name: Update Windows Apps
details: Review available updates and allow for app restarts.
UPDATE-WINDOWS-APPS.ps1.objective: Review and update installed applications using WinGet.

GET-USER-PREDELETE-CHECK.ps1.name: Check User Before Deletion
details: Collects dependencies to review before deletion.
Does not authorize or perform deletion.
GET-USER-PREDELETE-CHECK.ps1.objective: Review a user's mailbox, memberships, and access before deletion.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

INVOKE-ENFORCE-PER-USER-MFA.ps1.name: Set Per-user MFA
details: Per-user MFA is separate from Conditional Access.
Review the tenant's MFA approach before changing it.
INVOKE-ENFORCE-PER-USER-MFA.ps1.objective: Require per-user MFA for selected accounts after approval.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-ADMIN-ROLE-AUDIT.ps1.name: Audit Admin Roles
details: Review privileged assignments and their business owners.
GET-ADMIN-ROLE-AUDIT.ps1.objective: List tenant admin-role assignments for review.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-OAUTH-CONSENT-AUDIT.ps1.name: Audit App Consent
details: Review granted access and app ownership before removing consent.
GET-OAUTH-CONSENT-AUDIT.ps1.objective: Review app permissions granted in the tenant.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-GUEST-USER-AUDIT.ps1.name: Review Guest Users
details: Confirm the business relationship before removing a guest.
Missing activity is not proof that access is unused.
GET-GUEST-USER-AUDIT.ps1.objective: Find guest accounts that need an ownership or activity review.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-TENANT-LICENSING-AUDIT.ps1.name: Audit Tenant Licenses
details: Reviews assignments and capacity; does not change licenses.
GET-TENANT-LICENSING-AUDIT.ps1.objective: Review Microsoft 365 license capacity and user assignments.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-TENANT-INBOX-RULES-AUDIT.ps1.name: Audit Tenant Inbox Rules
details: Defaults to user mailboxes and all rules.
Use -IncludeShared to include shared mailboxes or -SuspiciousOnly to show flagged rules; these options require a terminal.
Investigate suspicious rules before removing them.
GET-TENANT-INBOX-RULES-AUDIT.ps1.objective: Find mailbox inbox rules that need review across the tenant.
preparation: Requires Exchange Online PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-USER-SECURITY-SNAPSHOT.ps1.name: Get User Security
details: A starting point for investigation, not an all-clear verdict.
GET-USER-SECURITY-SNAPSHOT.ps1.objective: Review one user's account, authentication, access, and recent sign-ins.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-TENANT-SECURITY-SNAPSHOT.ps1.name: Get Tenant Security
details: A broad starting point; use focused audits for follow-up.
GET-TENANT-SECURITY-SNAPSHOT.ps1.objective: Get a broad overview of the tenant's security settings and review areas.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-ROOM-RESOURCE-ACCESS.ps1.name: Get Resource Mailbox Access
details: Use an actual room or equipment mailbox, not a security group.
Enter one or more mailbox names or addresses, separated by commas. File input is not supported.
GET-ROOM-RESOURCE-ACCESS.ps1.objective: Review delegated access and booking permissions for resource mailboxes.
preparation: Requires Exchange Online PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-TENANT-MAILBOX-ACCESS-AUDIT.ps1.name: Audit Tenant Mailbox Access
details: Review unexpected forwarding or delegated access before changes.
GET-TENANT-MAILBOX-ACCESS-AUDIT.ps1.objective: Review mailbox forwarding and delegated access across the tenant.
preparation: Requires Exchange Online PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

CLEANUP-DISABLED-USER-MAILBOX-ACCESS.ps1.name: Remove Disabled User Mailbox Access
details: Checks one disabled user across mailboxes; does not process a list of users.
Review the removal plan before confirming.
CLEANUP-DISABLED-USER-MAILBOX-ACCESS.ps1.objective: Remove approved mailbox access held by one disabled user.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph and Exchange Online PowerShell with authorized tenant access.

GET-TENANT-DRIFT-REVIEW.ps1.name: Review Tenant Changes
details: If no baseline exists, asks before saving the current settings as a local baseline.
Investigate differences before replacing an existing baseline; a changed setting is not automatically an incident.
GET-TENANT-DRIFT-REVIEW.ps1.objective: Compare tenant settings with a saved baseline and review changes.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

GET-WINDOWS-STORAGE-CLEANUP-REVIEW.ps1.name: Review Windows Storage
GET-WINDOWS-STORAGE-CLEANUP-REVIEW.ps1.input: This computer; C: drive by default
details: Defaults to C: and the ten largest files; no files are deleted.
Use -ComputerName, -DriveLetter or -TopFiles in a terminal to change the scan. Remote scans require PowerShell remoting.
GET-WINDOWS-STORAGE-CLEANUP-REVIEW.ps1.objective: Find Windows storage that may be reclaimable without deleting files.

INVOKE-RESET-CLOUD-USER-PASSWORD.ps1.name: Reset Cloud User Password
details: Cloud-only accounts; synced accounts require their own identity process.
Handle temporary passwords securely; terminal recording may capture them.
INVOKE-RESET-CLOUD-USER-PASSWORD.ps1.objective: Reset passwords for selected cloud-only users after approval.
preparation: Requires Microsoft Graph PowerShell and authorized access to the target tenant.

ir-recover-validate.ps1.name: BEC: Restore and Validate
ir-recover-validate.ps1.input: User sign-in address and Microsoft 365 domain or tenant ID
details: Use the same workflow window and approved recovery decision.
Confirm sign-in and MFA before closing the incident.
ir-recover-validate.ps1.objective: Check recovery readiness and restore approved account access.
preparation: Use the approved Windows support computer with Microsoft.Graph.Authentication 2.x and ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.2+.

git-handoff.ps1.name: Save Project Handoff
details: Creates a screened project snapshot; review it before sharing.
git-handoff.ps1.objective: Save a screened snapshot of the current Git project for handoff.
preparation: Install Git for Windows before running.

git-repo.ps1.name: Manage Git Repository
details: Choose Check, Pull or Push when the launch command asks.
Check uses last-known remote state; it does not refresh it. Review the full diff before publishing.
git-repo.ps1.objective: Review, pull, or push changes in the selected Git repository.
preparation: Install Git for Windows before running.

git-security.ps1.name: Review GitHub Security
details: Reviews a downloaded JSON, JSON.GZ or ZIP export; does not sign in to GitHub.
A full review with no flags saves a local checkpoint. No findings is not an account-security verdict.
git-security.ps1.objective: Review a GitHub security-log export for unfamiliar access and activity.

set-execution.ps1.name: Set Up Script Execution
details: Place it beside only the reviewed scripts you intend to unblock.
Managed policies still apply.
set-execution.ps1.objective: Set local execution policy and unblock scripts beside this file.
set-execution.ps1.notice: May change your current-user execution policy. Unblocks every .ps1 file beside this file.

attractor.ps1.name: Attractor
details: Run in an existing terminal; use its own exit controls.
attractor.ps1.objective: Run a floating fractal animation with a clock.

rain.ps1.name: Rain
details: Run in an existing terminal; use its own exit controls.
rain.ps1.objective: Run animated terminal rain with a floating label and clock.

static.ps1.name: Static
details: Run in an existing terminal; use its own exit controls.
static.ps1.objective: Run animated terminal static with a floating label and clock.

SIGN-FOLDER-SCRIPTS.ps1.name: Sign Scripts
details: Review the selected certificate and files before signing.
A signature identifies the signer; it is not a code review.
SIGN-FOLDER-SCRIPTS.ps1.objective: Sign scripts in a selected folder with a code-signing certificate.
preparation: Have a usable code-signing certificate or approve creating one when prompted.

GET-TERMINAL-READINESS-CHECK.ps1.name: Check Toolkit Setup
details: Uses a fixed expected toolkit layout; a different layout can be intentional.
Reports missing prerequisites without repairing them.
GET-TERMINAL-READINESS-CHECK.ps1.objective: Check a toolkit folder against the expected files and setup.

INVOKE-FILE-INVENTORY.ps1.name: Compare Script Files
details: Compares file names and content hashes; does not delete duplicates.
Optional exports contain local paths and signer details. Review before sharing.
INVOKE-FILE-INVENTORY.ps1.objective: Compare script versions, signatures, and duplicate content in a folder.

INVOKE-MAP-KIT.ps1.name: Map Folder Structure
details: Shows folders and files up to the chosen depth.
Reports structure; does not enforce a layout or provide a complete secret scan.
INVOKE-MAP-KIT.ps1.objective: Show the folder structure and files beneath a selected location.

INVOKE-SESSION-RESET.ps1.name: Reset Terminal Session
details: Run in the session you want to reset.
INVOKE-SESSION-RESET.ps1.objective: Clear supported service connections from the current PowerShell session.

SET-THEME-BASIC.ps1.name: Preview Plain Output
details: Prints demonstration messages, not real connection or task results.
No startup theme is installed.
SET-THEME-BASIC.ps1.objective: Show a plain PowerShell output style without color.

SET-THEME-COBALT.ps1.name: Preview Cobalt Theme
details: No startup profile is installed. Close this PowerShell window to end session-only changes.
SET-THEME-COBALT.ps1.objective: Preview a blue PowerShell theme and output helpers.
SET-THEME-COBALT.ps1.notice: Changes this session’s appearance and sets Process execution policy to Bypass.

SET-THEME-SEAGLASS.ps1.name: Install Sea Glass Theme
details: Changes the current-user PowerShell profile and sets Process execution policy to Bypass.
Review the profile first. Remove the SEA GLASS THEME block to undo startup changes.
SET-THEME-SEAGLASS.ps1.objective: Install a sea-green PowerShell theme in your startup profile.
SET-THEME-SEAGLASS.ps1.notice: Installs a startup theme, replaces recognized theme blocks, and changes this session’s execution setting.

SET-THEME-SILICON-VALLEY.ps1.name: Install Silicon Valley Theme
details: Writes the current-user PowerShell profile.
Review the profile first. Remove the SILICON VALLEY THEME block to undo startup changes.
SET-THEME-SILICON-VALLEY.ps1.objective: Install a green PowerShell theme in your startup profile.
SET-THEME-SILICON-VALLEY.ps1.notice: Rewrites startup theme blocks and installs a predictable daily password generator. Never use its output as a password.

MANAGE-CERT-SIGNATURES.ps1.name: Manage Signing Certificates
details: Manages current-user signing certificates and related files.
Review the certificate before removal or export.
MANAGE-CERT-SIGNATURES.ps1.objective: Create, review, export, import, or trust script-signing certificates.
